newsitem.title: UK: UK's EMAP ousts rebel non-exec directors.
newsitem.headline: UK's EMAP ousts rebel non-exec directors.

text.p: Shareholders in British media group EMAP Plc voted on Monday to oust two rebel non-executive directors, who had contested changes to the company's articles, EMAP said in a statement.
Shareholders backed the board and voted overwhelmingly in favour of resolutions seeking the removal of dissidents Ken Simmonds and Joe Cooke in a poll called at an extraordinary general meeting.
More than 109.2 million votes were registered in favour of each of the two separate resolutions and 12.3 million against.

The row centred on changes removing a provision for a minimum of five non-executive directors and another allowing a director to be ousted on the vote of 75 percent of the board. Cooke and Simmonds opposed them, arguing that they transferred too much power from shareholders to the board.

Chairman Sir John Hoskyns told the meeting that the breakdown between the board and the dissidents was irreparable and that the removal of Cooke and Simmonds should end a row that has depressed the company's share price.
"I am confident that with these two resolutions passed, the board will be fully united and ready to give full attention to your company's business," he told shareholders.
